verdict.rationale: LiveKit Agents documents a first-party adaptive interruption handling feature that lets the agent respond naturally when users speak mid-response, and it acoustically separates intentional barge-ins from backchanneling. The turn detector also waits for users to finish speaking. Together these cover detecting a barge-in, but the evidence never shows what happens afterward. Missing for 10: explicit evidence that agent speech/TTS playback stops on barge-in, that conversation context is updated or truncated to what was actually spoken, that the agent recovers or resumes the turn after a false interruption, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can rely on the agent to handle interruptions (barge-in) gracefully — stopping speech, updating context, and recovering the turn

citations.quote: Adaptive interruption handling allows an agent to respond naturally when users speak mid-response.
the model analyzes the acoustic signals to identify intentional interruptions (barge-ins) from conversational backchanneling
A turn detector model can predict that they have more to say and wait for them to finish before responding.
